court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Lucknow in Case No. NIL of 2016
case_name: Rahul Verma vs Smt. Kiran Verma & 2 Others
facts_of_case: Divorce petition filed by Rahul Verma against Smt. Kiran Verma on various grounds including adulteration and desertion. Trial court rejected the petition on the ground that it is barred by Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The ground for desertion for claiming divorce under Section 13 (1) (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires that one spouse has been deserted by the other for a continuous period of two years immediately preceding the date of the presentation of the divorce petition.
legal_principles.held: After the amendment, the ground for desertion for claiming divorce under Section 13 (1) (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires that one of the spouse who has been deserted by the other for a continuous period of two years immediately preceding the date of the presentation of the divorce petition is entitled to a decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: The prescription of the continuous period of desertion for not less than two years signifies the intention of desertion and conduct of the party, burdening the onus of strict proof on the petitioner who claims that the other party has deserted him/her.
legal_principles.held: The prescription of the continuous period of desertion for not less than two years signifies the intention of desertion and conduct of the party, burdening the onus of strict proof on the petitioner who claims that the other party has deserted him/her.

outcome.final_order: The divorce petition was allowed and the trial court's decision was set aside.
